entry: ScalarValue is #[non_exhaustive]. The `_` arm in digest_step_primitive (part_05.rs:155) silently produces b"unsupported" for future variants. Compile-time exhaustion check is impossible due to #[non_exhaustive]. The code review checklist item 'When adding a ScalarValue variant, update digest_step_primitive' serves as the gate. The structural test scalarvalue_exhaustiveness_in_digest documents each current variant and compiles/runs with a panic for unknown variants.
mitigation: Exhaustiveness structural test + code review checklist. When a new variant is added, the test must be updated.

entry: Kani byte-level modeling for String encoding avoids UTF-8 validation overhead. The production code path is String::as_bytes() → hasher.update(bytes). Since String → bytes is identity (Rust invariant: distinct Strings have distinct byte buffers), proving byte-level injectivity (distinct [u8] arrays differ) is sound for the encoding property. The actual UTF-8 validation is trusted (Rust stdlib).
mitigation: Rust type system guarantee: String is uniquely determined by its UTF-8 bytes.

entry: Kani found a counterexample for the variant discrimination harness: a byte array of exactly 8 bytes can match an i64 LE encoding. For example, bytes [0x41, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] match i64 value 65. This requires a 8-byte String containing exact binary content of an i64 LE representation. Probability in real YAML workflow names: effectively zero. The blake3 collision resistance (2^-128) provides additional defense. The concept of a YAML output name matching an i64 LE pattern is semantically nonsensical in practice.
mitigation: Practically irrelevant edge case. blake3 collision resistance (2^-128) provides defense-in-depth. The separate String and Integer YAML parsing paths make this even less likely.

entry: Kani harnesses test encoding injectivity at the byte level without going through blake3::Hasher. This is sound per trusted-base-plan S-1: the proof is about distinct inputs to the hasher, not hash correctness. blake3 collision resistance is trusted (T-1). Proptest provides defense-in-depth against any mock/reality divergence.
mitigation: Proptest with real blake3 via compile_source provides defense-in-depth.

entry: canonical_digest() and digest_step_primitive() are pure functions. The grep audit confirms: no unsafe, no time, no random, no IO in part_05.rs lines 116-162. The only external dependency is blake3::Hasher. Function signature takes only &WorkflowSource (immutable AST reference). No runtime state, environment variables, or non-deterministic inputs.

REPAIR-2: Kani harnesses use MAX_BYTE_LEN=16 (not 256) due to Kani memcmp unwinding limitations on fixed-size arrays. The injectivity property is length-independent: if all byte sequences up to length N are injective under identity encoding, injectivity holds for any length N (the encoding preserves length and content). Proptest provides defense-in-depth with full-length strings through the real blake3 pipeline.
mitigation: Proptest with real blake3 via compile_source tests full-length inputs. Kani bound of 16 bytes is documented and justified.

entry: REPAIR-2: PO-KANI-FINISH-003 uses kani::assume(len != 8 || bytes[..8] != i.to_le_bytes()) to exclude the known 8-byte edge case (TB-FINISH-003) from the universal claim. Without this scoping, the assertion is mathematically false. The properly scoped claim is: for all inputs where the byte slice is NOT an exact 8-byte match with i64 LE, String and Integer Finish encodings differ. The edge case is accepted because it requires a semantically nonsensical YAML output name matching i64 LE binary pattern.
mitigation: Edge case documented in TB-FINISH-003. Integration test PO-INT-FINISH-003 provides defense-in-depth through real blake3 pipeline.

entry: REPAIR-2: Kani harnesses use encoding helpers (encode_finish_string_bytes, encode_finish_integer) that replicate digest_step_primitive's Finish arm byte-for-byte but return fixed-size arrays instead of Vec<Vec<u8>>. This avoids Kani memcmp unwinding issues on nested vector comparisons. The encoding logic is identical to production code: encode_finish_string_bytes mirrors part_05.rs:153, encode_finish_integer mirrors part_05.rs:154. If digest_step_primitive's Finish arm changes, these helpers MUST be updated to match.
mitigation: Proptest with real blake3 provides defense-in-depth against mock/reality divergence. Encoding helpers are documented with exact production line references.
